questions.question: What is ERB and how do you write it in Rails views?
questions.title: ERB Basics
questions.direct_answer: ERB (Embedded Ruby) is Rails' default templating language: it's HTML with Ruby sprinkled in using tags. <% ... %> runs Ruby (no output): <% @posts.each do |p| %>. <%= ... %> runs Ruby AND outputs the result: <%= @post.title %>. <% end %> closes a block. You use it to loop and display data: iterate with @posts.each, output with <%= p.title %>, interpolate with #{...} inside strings. Escape HTML by default (<%= %> escapes; use raw or html_safe to skip — only for trusted content). Keep views dumb: just show @vars the controller set; no business logic in the view.

interviewer_intent.testing: Whether you know <% %> (run, no output) vs <%= %> (run and output), and that <%= %> escapes HTML by default.
interviewer_intent.common_mistake: Using <% %> where you need output (nothing shows), or raw on untrusted content (XSS risk).
interviewer_intent.to_stand_out: ERB is HTML with Ruby: <% %> runs (no output), <%= %> runs + outputs (escapes HTML by default). Loop with each, output with <%=. Keep views dumb.

sections.title: HTML with Ruby Sprinkled In
sections.content: ERB (Embedded Ruby) is Rails' default templating language: it's HTML with Ruby sprinkled in using tags. Percent-angle run Ruby with no output: percent-equal runs Ruby AND outputs the result, like post dot title. percent end closes a block. You use it to loop and display data: iterate with posts dot each, output with the title, interpolate with hash-brace inside strings. Escape HTML by default — the output tag escapes; use raw or html_safe to skip, but only for trusted content. Keep views dumb: just show the instance vars the controller set; no business logic in the view.

sections.title: ERB Tags
sections.content:
<% %> runs (no output); <%= %> runs + outputs (escapes). <% end %> closes a block.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  A[<% ... %>: run, no output] --> B[<%= ... %>: run + output]
  B --> E[escapes HTML by default]
  E --> S[<% end %>: close block]
```

sections.title: ERB
sections.content:
```ruby

Posts

    <% @posts.each do |p| %>
  • <%= p.title %>
    • <% end %>

Total: <%= @posts.count %>

<% msg = "Found #{@posts.size} posts" %>

<%= msg %>

<%= user_input %> <%= raw user_input %> ```

sections.title: Common Mistakes
items: Using <% %> where you need output — nothing shows (use <%= %>).
Using raw or html_safe on untrusted content — XSS risk.
Business logic in the view — keep views dumb; logic in the model/controller.

sections.title: Key Takeaways
items: ERB is HTML with Ruby: <% %> runs (no output), <%= %> runs + outputs.
<% end %> closes a block (each, if); loop with @posts.each, output with <%= p.title %>.
raw or html_safe skips escaping — only for trusted content (else XSS).
Keep views dumb: show the @vars the controller set; no business logic in the view.

sections.title: Spoken Answer
sections.content: ERB (Embedded Ruby) is Rails' default templating language: it's HTML with Ruby sprinkled in using tags. Percent-angle run Ruby with no output: percent-equal runs Ruby AND outputs the result, like post dot title. percent end closes a block. You use it to loop and display data: iterate with posts dot each, output with the title, interpolate with hash-brace inside strings. Escape HTML by default — the output tag escapes; use raw or html_safe to skip, but only for trusted content. Keep views dumb: just show the instance vars the controller set; no business logic in the view. A common mistake is using the no-output tag where you need output, so nothing shows, and using raw on untrusted content, which is an XSS risk.
